# One-second technical-indicator predictiveness

Generated 2026-08-16T05:22:26.306Z. BTCUSDT indicators at close t predict the next one-second log return. The scan observes 157,766,399 returns and evaluates a deterministic one-in-4 sample: 39,438,595 total targets, 25,350,863 active.

## Result

At least one indicator adds material distributional information beyond the latest return state.

`Standalone` compares an indicator with no feature. `Incremental` compares history + indicator against the latest-return-state history alone. Positive bits mean better held-out probability forecasts.

## Interpretation

- The 33-state latest-return baseline is already strong: 0.57654057 bits/target over the unconditional full-return distribution. EMA slope(n=2s,k=2s) adds 0.10942173 bits beyond it in all four years, a 7.880% improvement in geometric assigned probability.
- Active sign is best served by EMA acceleration(n=2s,k=1s): 0.057973099 additional bits and 5.7437 percentage points of held-out sign accuracy beyond the latest return.
- The 16-cell active-magnitude distribution prefers EMA slope(n=2s,k=2s) (0.081476511 bits), while the conditional mean magnitude prefers Price−EMA(2048s): correlation rises from 0.29580839 to 0.39360475 and MSE falls 8.6897%.
- The signed conditional mean prefers RSI(2s): correlation rises from 0.044601280 to 0.086037821, with 0.6127% lower MSE.
- Among the new dynamics, EMA slope(n=2s,k=2s) is best for the full distribution at 0.10942173 bits. EMA slope(n=2s,k=2s) is best for active magnitude at 0.081476511 bits; both remain positive in all four years.
- Acceleration separates into two useful regimes: EMA acceleration(n=2s,k=1s) is strongest for sign (0.057973099 bits), while EMA acceleration(n=8192s,k=2s) is strongest for magnitude (0.080457405 bits). The latter changes only modestly from n=4096s to n=8192s, indicating slow-period saturation.
- The `k=1` EMA-slope control reproduces the corresponding Price−EMA metrics exactly across every target. This confirms the causal alignment and shows that the improvement starts specifically at the genuinely multi-step `k=2` slope.
- MACD is useful but dominated by the shortest RSI/EMA variants. Its best full-distribution result is MACD line(3,7,3) at 0.063519365 bits; longer MACD lines and histograms generally decay toward smaller gains.

## Method

- Causal alignment: Indicator at close t predicts log(close[t+1]/close[t]).
- Calibration: Indicator and active-magnitude equal-mass edges are fitted on year 0 only.
- Evaluation: Rolling annual holdout: each test year uses all earlier years, never later data.
- Feature quantization: 16 equal-mass cells; active magnitude: 16 equal-mass cells.
- Incremental baseline: Previous return: zero or sign crossed with 16 first-year magnitude cells.
- EMA uses alpha `2 / (period + 1)`; RSI uses Wilder alpha `1 / period`; MACD line and histogram are normalized by current price into basis points.

## Limitations

- This is a distributional predictiveness screen, not a fee-aware trading backtest.
- Indicator bin edges remain fixed after year 0, so later regime/scale drift is intentionally exposed rather than recalibrated away.
- Only every 4th target is scored to make the five-year hyperparameter sweep tractable; every candle still updates every causal indicator.
- Incremental scores condition on the immediately previous return state, not on every possible history representation or a trained neural model.
- The candidate grid creates multiple comparisons; annual consistency and effect size matter more than formal significance on the very large sample.

## Reproducibility

```text
node --conditions=development --import tsx scripts/analyze-technical-indicator-predictiveness.ts
```

The complete per-indicator, per-target, and per-year metrics are stored in `data/benchmarks/technical-indicator-predictiveness.json`.
